subject: maths
question: How many litres of water can a hemispherical bowl of radius 3 cm hold? (Use π = 3.14)
solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the hemispherical bowl = 3 cm

π = 3.14

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a hemisphere = (2/3) π r³

**Calculation:**

Volume of the bowl

⇒ (2/3) × 3.14 × 3³

⇒ (2/3) × 3.14 × 27

⇒ 56.52 cm³

Since 1 cm³ = 0.001 liters

⇒ 56.52 cm³ = 56.52 × 0.001 liters

⇒ 0.05652 liters

**The hemispherical bowl can hold 0.05652 liters of water.**
